transcript.text: My Shark cordless battery got really hot on charge last night and this morning it looks puffed up, the plastic case has split at the seam a bit. Can I still use it till a new one comes? It's the IZ201UK.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A swollen, very hot or chemical-smelling battery can catch fire. Stop using and charging it now, unplug the charger, and if it is safe to move put it somewhere non-flammable away from anything that could burn. Don't puncture, squeeze or try to open the battery, and don't put it in the household bin — take it to a battery recycling point. No — do not use or charge it again, even briefly. A battery that became very hot, has swollen and split its casing is unsafe and needs to be treated as failed until checked by a qualified engineer. The most likely cause is an internal lithium battery-cell failure. With everything switched off and unplugged:
1. Leave the battery out of the vacuum and away from anything flammable. 2. Do not put it in household bins or ordinary battery recycling. Contact Shark support or your local household-waste site for their damaged-lithium-battery disposal route; tell them it is swollen and heat-damaged.
3. Arrange a qualified inspection of the vacuum and charger before using either with another battery. This is not normal battery ageing, and it is not a fault that can be made safe by cleaning contacts or changing settings.

Ok, understood, I won't use it. It's currently leaning against the kitchen cupboards next to the tea towels and still clicked into the vacuum, and there's a bit of a chemical smell. What should I do with it right now?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Because it has a chemical smell as well as a split, swollen case, treat this as an immediate fire risk. 1. Keep people and pets out of the kitchen. Do not handle the battery, try to unclip it, or move the vacuum while it is against the cupboards.
2. Do not touch the charging contacts.
3. Move the tea towels and any other loose combustible items away from it, without disturbing the vacuum. Open an outside window if you can do so safely, to ventilate the room.
4. If it is hot now, smoking, hissing/crackling, leaking, or the smell is increasing: leave the kitchen, close the door behind you, get outside and call 999. Tell them there is a damaged, swollen lithium-ion vacuum battery with a chemical smell. Do not use the vacuum, charger or that battery again; all need professional assessment before any further use.

candidates: Failed lithium-ion battery pack / internal battery-cell fault (high)
Charging fault from charger or battery-management electronics (medium)

reading.symptom: battery got very hot while charging and has swollen, splitting the case

plan: They asked: "Can I still use it till a new one comes?" - answer that first.

Safety: a battery hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Shark; model IZ201UK.
The fault they reported is: "battery got very hot while charging and has swollen, splitting the case". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
